statement: For a characteristic-p point with perfect residue field k and a characteristic-zero point, compare the indicated crystalline fibre with the integral p-adic fibre extended to W(k). The author tentatively expects nonisomorphism in general but retains a qualified isomorphism assertion when k is finite; the final qualifier is uncertain. The tensor, integral, Frobenius and filtration structures to be preserved are not fully specified.
status_on_pages: Open on the pages; tentative wording, local deletions and an uncertain live finite-field exception.
computation: No numerical computation. See computations.md for any formal verification.
fate: Comparison theorems relate specified realizations after extending coefficients, but do not identify arbitrary integral or filtered fibre functors. Neither the general expectation nor the uncertain finite-field exception can be matched to one theorem with the manuscript’s unspecified category. Vasiu Main Theorem1.2 gives a stronger integral positive result for p-divisible groups over W(k) with k algebraically closed and specified crystalline tensors, with EC required at p=2. The comparison is W(k)-linear and tensor-compatible, suppressing the Galois action; it is not a comparison preserving all Frobenius and filtration data and does not settle the live finite-k exception.

his_statement: CL-SA07-009: τ=τ′τ″=τ″τ′; à vérifier | CL-SA07-411: sigma and tau commute; f=sigma tau
statement: Let X be a smooth proper variety over R and use its compatible Betti and algebraic de Rham realizations. On H_B(X(C),Q)⊗C let σ be coefficient conjugation, f∞ the rational Betti action induced by geometric conjugation, and τ the semilinear involution defining the de Rham real form. Comparison gives τ=f∞σ=σf∞. Hence στ=τσ=f∞ and f∞²=1. This uses the geometric comparison, not semilinearity alone; the finite-prime compatibility is a separate claim.
status_on_pages: Open on the pages at15/203 (à vérifier); stated without proof at18/033, with the geometric action and fixed-space explanation at18/035,037.
computation: p15/CL-SA07-009: C09 in code/compute_checks.py and §D2; counterexample concerns omission of geometric compatibility. | p18/CL-SA07-411: C02 and computations.md §2 model the two commuting real structures. This uses the comparison for an actual real variety, not arbitrary unrelated anti-linear involutions.
fate: The compatible geometric real structures give the identity by functoriality of comparison. Deligne’s real Hodge formalism supplies the published setting. The explicit counterexample to commutation of arbitrary semilinear involutions rules out the broader reading.
fate_date: Grothendieck comparison: letter1963-10-14, publication1966; Deligne Hodge formalism1971 and real-comparison exposition1982.
present_status: As of2026-11-19: established for the compatible realizations of a real variety; the geometry is an essential hypothesis.

statement: Assume a Q-linear rigid tensor category contains h¹(E) for a supersingular elliptic curve E over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, all its geometric endomorphisms, and would send h¹(E) to a two-dimensional real vector space under an ordinary fibre realization. Its endomorphism algebra is the quaternion algebra B_(p,∞), whose real scalar extension is Hamilton’s division algebra H. A faithful H-action on R² is impossible, since every nonzero H-module has real dimension divisible by4. Thus this category has no such R-valued fibre functor and no neutralization over a totally real number field. The nonneutral quaternionic model gerbe is a valid comparison target; it is not an ordinary real fibre functor. Smaller categories require separate analysis.
status_on_pages: Stated without proof for the Deuring real gerbe at15/052; open on the pages for sufficiently large motivic pieces and totally real extensions at15/207.
computation: p15/CL-SA07-013: C04; computations.md §D4 explains faithfulness, dimension2 and the all-endomorphisms hypothesis. | root/CL-SA07-721: root_computations.md §2: every nonzero finite-dimensional H-module has real dimension divisible by 4.
fate: Voight Theorem42.1.9 identifies the geometric supersingular endomorphism algebra. The real-module obstruction is independently re-proved in both package audits. It answers the explicit large-category question under the stated all-endomorphisms and dimension hypotheses, while preserving the page’s broader exploratory formulation.

his_statement: K_r=intersection of R_T; K_r algebraic over Q
statement: For an abstract field k isomorphic to C, intersect the inverse images of R over all field isomorphisms k→C. The result is the algebraic totally real closure of Q inside k: those algebraic elements whose every Q-conjugate is real.
status_on_pages: stated without proof
computation: computations.md §5 proves both inclusions using extension of embeddings and a transcendence basis; no choice of a single topology is silently fixed.
fate: This is a field-theoretic consequence of extension of embeddings. Searches for the manuscript formulation did not locate a separate theorem or publication; D71 addresses the distinct fixed-topology Hodge construction.
fate_date: Classical field theory before the sheet; no exact historical attribution established
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Valid for the full family of field isomorphisms. Restricting to one embedding or continuous automorphisms changes the statement.

present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Correct under the explicit hypotheses; no numerical result for the ambiguous literal reading is asserted.

his_statement: a coset of a finite-index subgroup contains a generic point at every l
statement: Let G/Q be geometrically connected smooth affine, K a compact open subgroup of its restricted adelic points, and U⊂K an open subgroup. Every coset of U contains an adelic point whose l-component is Q-generic in G for every prime l.
status_on_pages: stated without proof; admitted as an auxiliary lemma
computation: computations.md §8 gives a Baire-category proof: countably many rational proper subvarieties, each local zero set nowhere dense, and a compact product box inside the coset. Finite index alone needs closedness to imply openness.
fate: The argument reduces to classical Baire category and local analytic nonvanishing. Searches of the exact generic-coset phrase found no separately attributed theorem; CM20 supplies the modern adelic-openness context, not this proof.
fate_date: Classical ingredients; independent proof 2026-11-19
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Valid under the stated topological and geometric hypotheses; does not establish the preceding Galois-image premise.

his_statement: period point generic iff the actual cocycle image is Zariski dense
statement: Let P be a geometrically integral finite-type torsor over a finitely generated subfield k0⊂k≅C, and alpha∈P(k). The Aut(k/k0)-orbit of alpha is Zariski dense in P iff alpha is k0-generic. Translating the orbit by alpha identifies this with density of the actual comparison-cocycle image in G_k.
status_on_pages: proof sketched; presented as a reformulation of a period conjecture
computation: computations.md §11 proves the orbit assertion by algebraic loci and extension of field embeddings. C15 shows the subgroup generated by an image can be dense while the image is not.
fate: BC16 Cor2.11 and Conj2.12 distinguish point closure from generated period torsors. The conditional orbit equivalence is elementary field theory; genericity itself is the period conjecture, not a consequence of it.
fate_date: BC first preprint 2013; publication 2016
present_status: As of 2026-11-19: Equivalence valid with full Aut(k/k0), finite-type and geometric-integrality hypotheses. The general period genericity premise remains open.

statement: With “holomorphic” defined merely by a local power series at every point (B15-03, 15/057), uniqueness on a fixed open p-adic U is false. statement: For a closed analytic one-form in characteristic zero, compatibility of its partial derivatives determines a formal primitive by n_k b_n=c_{k,n−e_k}, with chosen constant. Hence the primitive converges locally. The claim concerns power-series germs, not uniqueness on disconnected p-adic domains.

his_statement: « il ne s’ensuit nullement … déformé … juxtaposition »
statement: The literal remark asserts that separately deformable path pieces need not have deformable concatenations. With unrestricted homotopy of interval maps this is false: H(t,s)=γ((1−s)t) contracts every path to its initial point, and the hypothesis places all relevant paths in the same path component. With endpoint-fixed individual homotopies concatenation is also valid. The narrower warning that two prescribed homotopies cannot be pasted unless their common endpoint tracks agree is valid (CL-SA07-742). A loop-preserving or prescribed-track interpretation would need an additional restriction absent from the supplied sentence.
